Chapter Three: Making Million-Dollar Decisions
Now that you’ve started shifting your mindset, let’s talk about something that really shapes your financial world—your everyday choices.
You know, wealth isn't usually the result of a big lottery win or some dramatic event. Instead, it's built one decision at a time—consistently, quietly, through what I like to call million-dollar decisions.
But here’s the thing… a million-dollar decision doesn’t always mean spending or saving a huge amount of money. Often, it’s about how you use your time, your energy, and where you put your attention.
Imagine this: every day, you’re standing at a fork in the road. One path leads toward more abundance, while the other keeps things just the way they are. When you keep choosing that growth path—even in small ways—it really adds up over time.
So, what do these million-dollar decisions actually look like?
Maybe it’s investing in your education or training, so you open new doors in your career. Or hiring some help—like a virtual assistant or a childcare provider—so you can spend more time on work that actually grows your income.
It could mean setting clear boundaries between work and home, so you avoid burnout and stay focused where it matters. Or, think about negotiating for better pay or benefits, instead of just taking the first offer that comes your way.
And don’t forget about prioritizing rest and self-care. After all, your well-being is the foundation for lasting success.
Of course, making these choices can feel uncomfortable at first. Saying no to others, spending money to buy back your time, or standing up for yourself—especially if you’re used to putting everyone else first—can seem risky.
But here’s the good news: every time you make a choice that supports your long-term growth, it gets a little bit easier. You start to build confidence, and soon, these decisions feel natural.
One tool that really helps? Try asking yourself, “Is this moving me closer to my financial goals, or further away?” That one question can cut through the noise and help you stay on track.
Now, not every decision is going to be spot-on. You’ll make mistakes, and that’s okay. Those moments are just opportunities to learn and try again.
Over time, making million-dollar decisions becomes second nature. And the real payoff? Not just more money—but greater confidence, freedom, and the ability to make a bigger impact with your life.
